basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'De terra illa egressus est Assur, et aedificavit Niniven, et plateas civitatis. De terra'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: De terra illa egressus est Assur, et aedificavit Niniven, et plateas civitatis. De terra illa, de terra Sennaar dicit, de qua Assyriorum pullulavit imperium, qui ex nomine Nini Beli filii Ninum condiderunt urbem magnam, quam Hebraei appellant Niniven. Sane quia tacere videtur Scriptura unde Assur ortus sit, a quo Assyriorum gens nasceretur, sed tantum de qua terra exierit ad construendam Niniven, vel alias quas commemorat civitates dicere, nonnulli Patrum intellexerunt hunc esse Assur filium Sem, de quo in sequentibus legitur. Sed sive idem, sive alius Assur fuerit, constat quia primum in terra regnum Babyloniorum, secundum Assyriorum, quorum metropolis erat Ninive, de eadem terra prodeuntium, fuerit.
